API E2E.Scenario: Find Owners page opens with an empty owner search form
API E2E.Given: The Petclinic application is running with the default seeded H2 data
API E2E.Then: The response is successful, the findOwners view is rendered, an owner model is available, and the Add Owner action is present
API E2E.Automation Notes: Use @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT) and an HTTP client that follows the real server boundary. Assert stable HTML markers instead of brittle full-page snapshots.

API E2E.Scenario: Last-name prefix with multiple owners renders the list page
API E2E.Given: The database contains Betty Davis and Harold Davis
API E2E.Then: The owners list page is rendered and both Davis owners are visible with address, city, telephone, and pet summaries
API E2E.Automation Notes: Verifies the business search contract for prefix matching through the complete web stack.

API E2E.Scenario: Last-name prefix with one owner redirects to owner details
API E2E.Given: The database contains a single seeded owner with last name Franklin
API E2E.Then: The response redirects to /owners/1 and the detail page shows George Franklin's contact information
API E2E.Automation Notes: Assert redirect first, then follow it and assert the detail fields and pets section.

API E2E.Scenario: Unknown last-name search returns the find form with a not-found validation message
API E2E.Given: No owner exists with a last name starting with Unknown Surname
API E2E.Then: The findOwners view is rendered, the lastName field has a notFound error, and no owner list table is shown
API E2E.Automation Notes: The existing controller slice covers the model error; E2E should confirm the rendered user-facing behavior.

API E2E.Scenario: Valid owner creation persists the owner and redirects to details with a success message
API E2E.Given: A unique new owner payload with first name, last name, address, city, and a 10-digit telephone
API E2E.When: A user posts the payload to POST /owners/new
API E2E.Then: The response redirects to the new owner detail page, the detail page shows the submitted values, and the success message says New Owner Created
API E2E.Automation Notes: Seed a unique last name per test and clean up via repository after the assertion because RANDOM_PORT server transactions do not roll back automatically.

API E2E.Scenario: Invalid owner creation returns the form and does not create a database row
API E2E.Given: A new owner payload is missing address and has a telephone that is not exactly 10 digits
API E2E.When: A user posts the payload to POST /owners/new
API E2E.Then: The create owner form is rendered again, field validation errors are shown, and no owner row is persisted for the submitted last name
API E2E.Automation Notes: Assert both rendered validation and repository absence. This covers Bean Validation through the real MVC binding path.

API E2E.Scenario: Owner details page shows owner contact data, pets, visits, and owner actions
API E2E.Given: Owner 6 has two cats and seeded visits
API E2E.Then: The ownerInformation page shows Jean Coleman's address, city, telephone, pets in name order, visits in date order, and links to edit the owner, add a pet, edit pets, and add visits
API E2E.Automation Notes: Good full-stack regression for owner aggregate rendering with spring.jpa.open-in-view=false.

API E2E.Scenario: Valid owner update persists changed contact fields and redirects with a success message
API E2E.Given: An existing owner is created for the test
API E2E.When: A user posts changed address, city, and telephone values to POST /owners/{ownerId}/edit
API E2E.Then: The response redirects to the owner detail page, the updated values are visible, and the success message says Owner Values Updated
API E2E.Automation Notes: Create a throwaway owner for this E2E and delete it after the test. Avoid mutating seeded owners.

API E2E.Scenario: Unknown owner detail request renders the application error response
API E2E.Then: The application returns an error response and does not render an owner detail page for a different owner
API E2E.Automation Notes: Current controller throws IllegalArgumentException. Capture the current error contract, or mark invalid if product wants a friendlier 404 before automation.

Integration.Scenario: Blank last-name repository search supports deterministic pagination
Integration.Given: The seeded database contains ten owners
Integration.When: OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith is called with an empty string and PageRequest.of(0, 5)
Integration.Then: The page contains five owners, reports totalElements 10, and the first page can be distinguished from the second page
Integration.Automation Notes: Protects the controller's parameterless /owners behavior and the fixed page-size contract.

Integration.Scenario: Saving a new owner generates an ID and persists all contact fields
Integration.Given: A transient Owner with valid first name, last name, address, city, and 10-digit telephone
Integration.When: The owner is saved and reloaded through OwnerRepository
Integration.Then: The owner has a generated ID and all submitted fields are persisted exactly
Integration.Automation Notes: Use @DataJpaTest transaction rollback for isolation. Existing coverage asserts ID and count; this scenario adds exact field round-trip assertions.

Integration.Scenario: Updating owner contact fields preserves existing pet relationships
Integration.Given: An existing seeded owner has one or more pets
Integration.When: The owner contact fields are updated and saved through OwnerRepository
Integration.Then: The changed owner fields are persisted and the existing pets remain associated with the owner
Integration.Automation Notes: Existing coverage updates lastName only. Add relationship preservation to catch accidental cascade or form-binding regressions.

Integration.Scenario: Reloaded owner aggregate contains pets sorted by name and visits sorted by date
Integration.Given: A seeded owner has multiple pets and visits
Integration.When: The owner is loaded through OwnerRepository.findById
Integration.Then: The pets collection is ordered by pet name and each pet's visits are ordered by visit date ascending
Integration.Automation Notes: Validates @OrderBy on Owner.pets and Pet.visits plus eager aggregate loading used by the detail page.

Integration.Scenario: Owner Bean Validation rejects missing names, address, city, and invalid telephone
Integration.Given: An Owner object has blank required fields and telephone values that are not exactly ten digits
Integration.When: The Jakarta Validator validates the owner
Integration.Then: Validation violations are returned for firstName, lastName, address, city, and telephone
Integration.Automation Notes: Can also be implemented as a focused unit-style validation test using the existing ValidatorTests pattern if preferred.

Integration.Scenario: Owner update ignores mass-assignment attempts for owner ID and nested pet IDs
Integration.Given: An existing owner has at least one pet
Integration.When: A form post to /owners/{ownerId}/edit includes id and pets[0].id parameters that differ from the existing aggregate
Integration.Then: The owner ID and nested pet IDs remain unchanged, and only allowed owner contact fields are updated
Integration.Automation Notes: Targets OwnerController.setAllowedFields, which disallows id and *.id. Use MockMvc with a real repository or a repository spy depending on the final harness.

Integration.Scenario: Mismatched owner model ID does not save and redirects back to edit
Integration.Given: The URL ownerId is 1 but the bound owner object has ID 2
Integration.Then: The response redirects to /owners/1/edit, an error flash attribute is added, and OwnerRepository.save is not called
Integration.Automation Notes: Existing controller test checks redirect and flash only; add no-save verification if this scenario is approved.

Unit.Given: An owner has one transient pet and one pet with an existing ID
Unit.When: Owner.addPet is called for both pets
Unit.Then: Only the transient pet is added to the owner pets collection
Unit.Automation Notes: Pure unit test with no Spring context. Documents the domain helper's isNew guard.

Unit.Scenario: Owner.getPet by name is case-insensitive and returns null when absent
Unit.Given: An owner has a pet named Max
Unit.When: Owner.getPet is called with max, MAX, and Unknown
Unit.Then: The first two lookups return Max and the unknown lookup returns null
Unit.Automation Notes: Fast domain regression that does not duplicate controller behavior.

Unit.Scenario: Owner.getPet by name can ignore new unsaved pets
Unit.Given: An owner has an unsaved pet named Max and a saved pet named Buddy
Unit.When: Owner.getPet("Max", true) and Owner.getPet("Max", false) are called
Unit.Then: The ignoreNew lookup returns null and the normal lookup returns the unsaved Max pet
Unit.Automation Notes: Targets logic used by duplicate-pet-name validation flows.

Unit.Scenario: Owner.getPet by ID ignores unsaved pets and matches saved IDs
Unit.Given: An owner has one unsaved pet and one saved pet with ID 7
Unit.Then: The ID 7 lookup returns the saved pet and null lookup does not match the unsaved pet
Unit.Automation Notes: Documents current null/unsaved semantics without requiring a database.

Unit.Given: An owner has a saved pet
Unit.When: Owner.addVisit is called with a null pet ID or a null Visit
Unit.Then: An IllegalArgumentException is thrown with a useful validation message
Unit.Automation Notes: Spring Assert.notNull throws IllegalArgumentException. Assert messages to preserve diagnostics.

Unit.Scenario: Owner.addVisit rejects an unknown pet ID
Unit.Given: An owner has a saved pet with ID 7
Unit.When: Owner.addVisit is called with pet ID 999
Unit.Then: An IllegalArgumentException is thrown and no visit is added to any pet
Unit.Automation Notes: Covers the Invalid Pet identifier guard before mutating pet visits.

Unit.Scenario: Owner.addVisit adds a visit to the requested pet only
Unit.Given: An owner has two saved pets with different IDs
Unit.When: Owner.addVisit is called for the second pet ID
Unit.Then: Only the second pet receives the visit and the first pet's visits remain unchanged
Unit.Automation Notes: Fast critical unit coverage for owner-to-pet visit routing.

Unit.Scenario: Owner telephone accepts exactly ten digits and rejects separators, letters, and short values
Unit.Given: Owners are created with telephone values 0123456789, 012-345-6789, abcdefghij, and 12345
Unit.Then: Only the exactly ten-digit telephone is valid
Unit.Automation Notes: Complements API validation by directly locking the @Pattern contract on Owner.telephone.
